Paper_Set_079.q: The Benioff zone is found along which type of plate boundaries?
Paper_Set_079.explanation: (b) : Destructive plate boundaries – A rigid landmass is called a plate. The study of the nature and movement of these plates is known as plate tectonics. The plate tectonics theory was introduced by Harry Hess in 1960, but its scientific explanation is credited to W.J. Morgan. The Benioff zone is found along destructive plate boundaries. When two plates collide, the denser plate subducts beneath the less dense plate. The region where the plate sinks is called the subduction zone. Since the plate is being destroyed in this area, it is called a destructive plate boundary.

Paper_Set_079.q: The recurrence of anticyclonic weather conditions is characteristic of which region?

Southern Hemisphere. Anticyclones are usually 
circular but can sometimes appear in an elongated 
shape. The air pressure at the center is higher, 
decreasing outward, causing winds to move from the 
center to the periphery. The term "anticyclone" was 
first introduced by Francis Galton in 1860.

Paper_Set_079.q: Who among the following has included both empirical and genetic classification in the world climate classification?
Paper_Set_079.explanation:
In the classification of world climate, G.T. 
Trewartha incorporated both empirical and genetic 
classifications, whereas Koppen and Thornthwaite’s 
classifications are empirical. Trewartha modified 
Koppen’s system to develop his own, which combined 
empirical (based on observation) and genetic (based on 
causation) elements. His main objective was to simplify 
classification so that only a few main climate types 
could be identified across the globe. He did not favor a 
large number of climate types. Like Koppen, he used 
temperature and rainfall as the basis of classification. 
He identified six primary climate types at the global 
level, labeled as A, B, C, D, E, and H. Among these, the 
"B" climate type was based on rainfall, while the others 
were primarily based on temperature.

Paper_Set_080.q: Identify correct statements with reference to tropical cyclones. A. The hurricane level cyclones have at least 119 kilometers' per hour wind speeds. B. Paper_Set_080.explanation:
Tropical cyclones are generated between 
approximately 5° and 30° latitudes in both hemispheres. 
The Coriolis force has no effect at the equator; 
therefore, even though the pressure is low, winds do not 
circulate in a spiral manner and cyclones do not form 
there. Cyclones also do not cross the equator. In 
different parts of the world, tropical cyclones are known 
by different names. For example, in the North Atlantic 
Ocean—especially the Caribbean Sea and the 
southeastern United States—they are called hurricanes. 
Hurricanes move at speeds of around 120 km per hour. 
In the northern Indian Ocean, especially the Bay of 
Bengal around 30° N latitude, tropical cyclones occur 
more frequently than in the southern Indian Ocean. It is 
noteworthy that due to global warming, the frequency 
of tropical cyclones has increased, not decreased.

Paper_Set_080.q:

 Statement (R): Cooling and contraction helped the Earth assume a tetrahedral shape.
options: Both A and R are correct, and R correctly explains A.

Paper_Set_080.explanation: (a) : Tetrahedral Hypothesis was given by Lowthian Green. According to this theory if sphere is subjected to uniform pressure on all sides, it would be transformed in shape of tetrahedron. • Initially, Earth very hot-Cooling began-first outer part cooled and it led to the formation of crust & inner part continued cooling. • Consequently, Inner part was subjected to more contraction due to continued cooling & reduction in volume of inner part. • Consequently, upper part collapsed on the inner part & earth began to assume the shape of the tetrahedron. • As per the theory, Oceans represent the plain faces of the tetrahedron and landmasses represent Apices & in case of earth, apices are not much sharpened, rather they are flat and convex. • Four oceans (Arctic, Atlantic, Pacific & Indian ocean) were formed on 4 plane faces of tetrahedron. • Upper flat face- Arctic Ocean & other 3-Pacific, Atlantic & Indian Ocean • 3 Vertical Edges- N & S Americas, Europe & Africa, & Asia. • Lower Point- Antarctica. • Three Apices are located in N. HEM (Canadian Shield, Baltic Shield & Siberian Shield) & fourth one in S.HEM (Pivot-Antarctic Shield). • Therefore, present continents have grown out of these shields represented by Apices of Tetrahedron.

Thursday = 32°C 
 Total temp = 3 × 32°C = 96°C 
Average temp of Wednesday, Thursday and Friday 
 = 34°C 
 Total temp = 3×34°C = 102°C 
 Temp on Tuesday = 30°C 
⇒ Temp on (Wednesday + Thursday + Friday) – 
 (Tuesday + Wednesday + Thursday) 
 = 102°C – 96°C 
 Friday – Tuesday = 6°C 
 Friday = 6°C + Tuesday = 6°C + 30°C 
 Temp. on Friday = 36°C

Paper_Set_080.explanation: (b) : The Aleutian Islands in the North Pacific Ocean are sites of volcanic eruptions because they are located at a destructive (convergent) plate boundary. Here, two plates converge, and the heavier plate subducts beneath the lighter one. Such destructive or convergent plate margins are common sites of volcanism. About 80% of volcanic activity occurs along destructive plate boundaries, while about 15% occurs along constructive plate boundaries. Nearly two-thirds of the world’s volcanoes are found along the coasts, island arcs, and oceanic islands surrounding the Pacific Ocean. This chain of volcanoes is known as the Pacific Ring of Fire.

These areas typically occur where there are strong temperature gradients, which are often found along the edges of mountains. The areas east of the Sierra Nevada mountains, along with the areas east of the Canadian Rockies and in Eastern Colorado are all Known to be locations where these contrasting air masses meet and front genesis occurs. However, the area west of the Sierra Nevada is generally characterized by a more uniform climate with less pronounced temperature gradients, making it less prone to frontogenesis.

Paper_Set_081.q: Who emphasized the thermal influence of the Tibetan Plateau on monsoon origin?
Paper_Set_081.explanation:

Plateau, which rises 5 km into the atmosphere, absorbs 
more solar radiation and heats up significantly during 
summer. This creates a thermal anticyclone above it, 
weakening the western subtropical jet stream south of 
the Himalayas while forming an eastern jet stream. 
Initially, this jet stream emerges over eastern India but 
later shifts westward, extending over India, the Arabian 
Sea, and East Africa. This process strengthens the high
pressure system over the Indian Ocean, leading to the 
onset of the southwest monsoon.

The classification of the physical

India is divided into four major physiographic regions

Paper_Set_082.q: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? (Economic Activity) – (Activity Type)
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
The correct classifications are: 
• Tertiary sector – Business 
• Secondary sector – Manufacturing 
• Primary sector – Hunting and gathering 
• Quaternary sector – Information and research 
Secondary activities include industries that transform 
raw materials into finished products, such as 
manufacturing textiles from cotton or producing steel 
from iron ore.

Paper_Set_082.q: Match List-1 with List-2 and choose the correct answer using the code below: List-I List-II A Trophic level 1 I Carnivores B Trophic level 2 II Autotrophs C Trophic level 3 III Primary consumers D Trophic level 4 IV Decomposers A B C D
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
In ecological food chains, autotrophs are at 
the first level, primary consumers at the second, 
secondary consumers at the third, and decomposers at 
the fourth.

Paper_Set_082.q: Which of the following rivers does not form a delta?
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
The Tapti river flows westwards and falls into 
the Arabian sea. Its valley is deep and narrow and it 
forms an estuary, not a delta.

Paper_Set_082.q: Assertion (A) and Reason (R): Assertion (A): The ozone hole is visible over the South Pole. Reason (R): Ozone-depleting gases are present throughout the stratosphere. Which of the following is correct?
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
The ozone hole is primarily found over the 
Antarctic region (South Pole) due to unique 
atmospheric conditions. 
While ozone-depleting substances (CFCs, halons) exist 
globally, their highest impact is at the South Pole due to 
extreme cold.

Paper_Set_082.q: Why are most of Britain's iron and steel factories located near seaports?
options: Convenience of disposing of waste into the sea
Availability of secure locations for factories
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
Most of Britain's iron and steel factories are 
located near seaports because they depend on imported 
iron ore.

After which publication did the concept of "Lebensraum" (Living Space) become popular in political geography?
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
The concept of "Lebensraum" was first 
proposed by Friedrich Ratzel in his book Politische 
Geographie. 
• Ratzel considered the state as a biological entity. 
• He is also known as the father of political 
geography.

Paper_Set_082.q: Which statement(s) is/are correct regarding Spykman's Rimland theory? 1. Rimland was considered to be located mainly in the central part of Russia. 2. Rimland is the cause of world conflict.
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
Regarding Spykman's Rimland theory only 
Statement (2) Rimland is the cause of world conflict is 
correct.

Paper_Set_082.q: Which Indian state does not fall under Seismic Zone V (the highest seismic risk zone)?
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
Madhya Pradesh does not fall under India's 
Seismic Zone V (the highest risk zone). 
• The point within the Earth where an earthquake 
originates is called the hypocenter. 
• The point directly above it on the surface where the 
seismic waves first reach is called the epicenter. 
• The instrument used to record seismic waves is 
called a seismograph.

Paper_Set_082.q: Which of the following geographers is related to human geography?
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
Vidal de la Blache contributed to both 
human and physical geography. Humboldt focused 
more on physical geography, while Davis and Penck 
were primarily physical geographers.

Paper_Set_082.q: Who is considered the pioneer of urban geography in India?
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
R.L. Singh is considered the pioneer of 
urban geography in India.

Paper_Set_082.q: In the sight of Kant, Geography is–
Paper_Set_082.explanation: (a) : Kant was the first who provided an early statement of geography as chorology. Chorology is the areal distribution of geographical phenomena over a particular region on the surface of earth. Chorology is essential and indispensable components of regional geography.

Paper_Set_082.q: Consider the following statements: Assertion (A): The literacy rate among Scheduled Castes in Kerala is higher than the national average. Reason (R): Scheduled Castes in Kerala are sufficiently prosperous. Options:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) correctly explains (A).2
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) does not correctly explain (A).
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
The high literacy rate among Scheduled 
Castes in Kerala is not due to prosperity but because of 
the efforts of Christian missionaries and local social, 
religious, and ethnic organizations in spreading 
education.

Paper_Set_082.q: Which of the following is a footloose industry?
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
Footloose industries can be set up anywhere 
depending on demand, e.g., hosiery and electronics.

Paper_Set_082.q: How many essential elements do plants need?
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
Plants require 16 essential elements for 
complete development. 
 Note: The commission considered the answer to be (c) 
16, but in fact, the correct number is 18.

Paper_Set_082.q: Horse Latitudes are located approximately at which latitude north and south of the equator?
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
Horse latitudes are located around 30° 
latitude north and south of the equator.

Paper_Set_082.q: Which country has the largest amount of arable land?
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
India has the second-largest area of 
agricultural land after the United States. Various types 
of crops are cultivated in India, making it an 
agriculture-based country.

Paper_Set_082.q: Which of the following is not an effect of ozone depletion?
options: Increase in rainfall and soil moisture
Adverse effects on species in ecosystems
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
Increase in rainfall and soil moisture is not 
related to ozone depletion. 
The ozone layer absorbs harmful UV radiation, 
protecting all life forms. Ozone depletion can lead to: 
• Reduced immunity in humans 
• Increase in global temperature 
• Negative impact on biodiversity 
• Glacier melting and rising sea levels leading to 
flooding in coastal areas.

Paper_Set_082.q: Who first proposed the Theory of Industrial Location?
Paper_Set_082.explanation:

formulate the Theory of Industrial Location in

Paper_Set_082.q: Identify the correct statements about Central Place Theory A. The range of goods is the maximum distance that a consumer is willing to travel to obtain certain good service. B. Having a high order service implies that there are low order services around it, and vice versa. C. In transport principle for each higher order centre, there are three centres of immediate lower order. D. The larger the town, the larger is its complementary area. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
The range of a good or service is the 
maximum distance consumers are willing to travel to 
obtain it. The presence of higher-order services implies 
nearby lower-order services are available, but there is 
no compulsory relationship. In central place theory, 
each higher-order center has four nearest lower-order 
centers. The larger the city, the greater its 
complementary area. The Central Place Theory was 
formulated by German economist Walter Christaller in 
his book Central Places in Southern Germany, which 
calculated population, distances, and areas using a 
hexagonal model.

Paper_Set_082.q: Who is the author of Erdkunde?
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
Carl Ritter is the author of Erdkunde. 
• Ritter was a theist and teleological thinker. 
 Erdkunde means "Science of the Earth" and 
consists of 14 volumes, primarily describing 
Africa and Asia.

Paper_Set_082.q: The vertical difference in height between low tide and high tide is referred to as:
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
Tidal range 
The tidal range is the vertical difference between 
high tide and low tide levels. 
Typically, there are two high tides and two low tides 
daily at most locations. 
However, tides do not follow an exact 12-hour cycle 
and occur 26 minutes later each day due to the 
Moon's orbit around Earth. 
Low tide (ebb) follows high tide (flood) 
approximately 6 hours and 13 minutes later.

Paper_Set_082.q: Which of the following is known as a producer in marine ecology?
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
Phytoplankton is known as a producer in 
marine ecology. It is important to note that all green 
plants are considered producers as they perform 
photosynthesis, converting CO2 and water into glucose 
in the presence of chlorophyll and sunlight.

Paper_Set_082.q: The largest rice-producing and exporting countries in the world are respectively:
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
According to updated data from 2020, the largest 
rice-producing countries in the world are China, India, 
Bangladesh, and Indonesia, while the largest exporting 
countries are India, Thailand, and Pakistan. Hence, China 
and India are the leading rice producers and exporters.

Paper_Set_082.q: 'Frontal wave theory' was propounded by:
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
Frontal wave theory was propounded by 
Norwegian meteorologist Vilhelm Bjerknes in early 20th 
century. This theory describes the formation and evolution 
of multitude cyclones along atmospheric fronts, which are 
boundaries between contrasting air masses.

Paper_Set_082.q: Which one of the following fault has greater risk of landslides ?
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
Reverse fault has greater risks of landslides 
because it is a dip-slip fault in which the upper block, 
above the fault plane, moves up and over the lower 
block. This type of faulting is common in areas of 
compression, such as regions where one plate is being 
subducted under another.

Paper_Set_082.explanation:

Plains → Terai → Bhabar → Mountains

Paper_Set_082.q: Where is the headquarters of the European Union located?
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
The headquarters of the European Union is 
located in Brussels, Belgium. The European Union was 
established in 1993.

Paper_Set_082.q: The dust and the ash material that comes out of a volcano is called as–
Paper_Set_082.explanation: (a) : Pyroclast. Pyroclastic materials thrown during explosive type of eruption are grouped into three categories (i) Essential materials (ii) Accessory materials (iii) Accidental materials. On the basis of size, pyroclastic materials are grouped into (i) Volconic dust (ii) Volconic ash (iii) Lapilli (iv) Volcanic bombs.

Paper_Set_082.q: Which mineral is primarily used for nuclear energy production?
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
Uranium is the primary mineral used for 
nuclear energy production. 
• Major uranium ores include Uraninite and 
Pitchblende. 
• Kazakhstan is the largest producer of uranium. 
• India's uranium reserves are found in Singhbhum, 
Udaipur, Jaipur, Nellore, Palakkad, and Shillong 
Plateau.

Paper_Set_082.q: Which state has the highest potential irrigation capacity?
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
Uttar Pradesh has the highest created irrigation 
potential (25.7 million hectares), followed by Bihar, 
Andhra Pradesh, Punjab, and Madhya Pradesh.

Paper_Set_082.q:
As per the Elastic Rebound Theory, tectonic earthquakes are closely associated with which of the following activities?
 1. Faulting
 2. Folding
 3. Volcanic
 Select the correct answer using code given below
 Code
Paper_Set_082.explanation: (a) : The Elastic Rebound Theory was proposed by Harry Fielding Reid after the 1906 San Francisco earthquake. • According to this theory, earthquakes occur due to the sudden release of accumulated stress along faults. • According to this theory, tectonic earthquakes are closely associated with faulting. As tectonic plates move, stress builds up along faults until it exceeds the strength of the rocks, causing a sudden rupture and release of energy in the form of seismic waves.

Paper_Set_082.q: Which type of soil has the largest coverage in India?
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
Alluvial soil has the largest coverage in 
India. It covers approximately 43.4% (around 1.5 
million square kilometers) of the total land area. This 
soil is spread across the vast plains from Punjab to 
Assam, as well as in the valleys of the Narmada, Tapi, 
Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri rivers, along 
with coastal areas of Kerala. Other soil types include 
red soil (18.6%), black soil (15.2%), laterite soil 
(3.7%), and other soils (17.9%).

Paper_Set_082.q: In which state was the average annual growth rate of population higher than the national growth rate between 1991-2001?
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
During the specified period, Jammu & 
Kashmir had a higher annual growth rate than the 
national growth rate. According to the 2011 Census, the 
population growth rate in Jammu & Kashmir was 
29.43%, Assam 18.92%, Odisha 16.25%, and Punjab 
20.10%.

Paper_Set_082.q: Which of the following is a planned city?
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
Kolkata, New Delhi, and Mumbai have 
ancient inhabited areas influenced by their strategic 
location, while Chandigarh is a planned city. Its plan was 
made in 1950 by Albert Mayer, and Le Corbusier made 
improvements in 1951. Construction began in 1952.

Paper_Set_082.q: Who proposed the Hydraulic Slope Theory?
Paper_Set_082.explanation: (c) : The Hydraulic Slope Theory was proposed by R. E. Horton.

Paper_Set_082.q: In which Indian state is the highest sugarcane yield per acre recorded?
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
According to the Fourth Advance Estimates 
of 2019-20, Tamil Nadu has the highest sugarcane yield 
per acre. However, in terms of total sugarcane 
production, Uttar Pradesh ranks first, followed by 
Maharashtra and Karnataka. Globally, about one-third 
of the world's sugarcane is produced in India.

Paper_Set_082.q: Which of the following regions is an example of a pseudo-monsoon?
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
In this region, there are distinct seasons of 
winter, summer, and rainfall. 
• Summer temperatures exceed 27°C. 
• Winter temperatures drop to around 10°C. 
• Annual temperature variation is about 15°C. 
• Rainfall occurs immediately after summer. 
• Winters are mostly dry, with annual rainfall ranging 
from 40 cm to 200 cm.

Paper_Set_082.q: Which of the following is not a process of cultural change?
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
Segregation is not a process of cultural 
change, while acculturation, diffusion, and innovation 
are processes that contribute to cultural transformation.

Paper_Set_082.q: How long does it take for sunlight to reach the Earth?
Paper_Set_082.explanation:
Sunlight takes 8 minutes 16.6 seconds to 
reach the Earth. The Sun, which is the primary 
Atmosphere 243component of the solar system, rotates from west to east 
on its axis. The energy we receive from the Sun is 
produced through nuclear fusion. The Sun is 
approximately 4.5 billion years old, and after 
exhausting its energy, it will become a red giant.

Paper_Set_083.q: A sharp-edged glacially eroded ridge is called as:
Paper_Set_083.explanation: (d) : A sharp-edged glacially eroded ridge is called as arete. Arete is an erosional glacial landform.

Net primary production is the amount of energy or biomass stored after losses.
Primary productivity is usually measured in grams per square meter per year.
Biomass refers to the wet weight of living organisms in a given area at any given time.
Paper_Set_083.explanation:
Biomass refers to the dry weight of living 
organisms, not the wet weight.

Moscow - Shipbuilding

Paper_Set_083.q: 'Bhabar' is an example of–
Paper_Set_083.explanation: (b) : A plain formed by river deposition is typically referred to as an alluvial plain. When a river descends from hilly areas into a lower region, the sudden decrease in slope prevents the larger rock fragments carried by the river from moving further, leading to the formation of an alluvial fan. When multiple alluvial fans merge to form an extensive plain, it is called a piedmont plain. In India, these piedmont plains are known as ‘Bhabar.’

Paper_Set_083.q: The Aral Sea is located on the border of which two countries?
Paper_Set_083.explanation:
The Aral Sea is located between Kazakhstan 
and Uzbekistan. 
• It is a saltwater lake. 
• The deepest lake in the world is Lake Baikal, while 
the largest lake by area is the Caspian Sea.

Paper_Set_083.q: In developing countries, migration increases population pressure in certain areas. What is the main characteristic of such areas?
Paper_Set_083.explanation:
Migration increases population pressure in 
certain areas of developing countries due to the 
availability of better employment opportunities.

Paper_Set_083.q: Who among the following explained the north-south positioning of the Rockies and Andes on the western edge of North and South America through his "drift or displacement" theory?
Paper_Set_083.explanation: (c) : F. B. Taylor explained the north-south positioning of the Rockies and Andes on the western edge of North and South America through his drift or displacement theory. The possibility of continental drift was first suggested by Antonio Snyder in 1858. Later, in 1910, Taylor attempted to explain the distribution of folded mountains based on the concept of continental drift. However, it was Wegener who formally presented the theory of continental drift in 1912.

Paper_Set_083.q: Mauna Loa is an active volcano in?
Paper_Set_083.explanation: (c) : Hawaii Island. Mauna Loa is an active Volcano, Located on Hawaii Island. It covers about half of Hawaii Island.

Paper_Set_083.q: There are some countries which possess a large number of the world's species diversity called as 'mega diversity centers'. These are situated in which of the following regions.
Paper_Set_083.explanation:
The tropical region is the region with the 
highest species diversity in the world, it is also called 
the 'Centre of Mega diversity'. This region provides 
optimum conditions for the development and growth of 
plants and animals.

Paper_Set_083.q: Which one of the following rivers and associated projects is correctly matched in terms of location of projects in correct sequence from upper course to lower course of river?
options: Narmada River : Omkareshwar Dam – Narmada Sagar Dam – Sardar Sarovar Dam.
Chambal River : Gandhi Sagar – Jawahar Sagar – Rana Pratap Sagar.
Satluj River : Nathpa Jhakri – Harike Barrage – Bhakhra Dam.
Damodar River : Tenughat – Panchet – Durgapur Barrage.
Paper_Set_083.explanation: (d) : The correct answer is : (d) Damodar River :- Tenughat - Panchet- Durgapur barrage • Tenughat dam is located in the upper reaches of Damodar River in Jharkhand. Panchet dam is downstream from Tenughat, located near Dhanbad. Durgapur Barrage is further downstream in west Bengal, built for irrigation and water supply.

Paper_Set_083.q: Why is the Indian Ocean region geopolitically significant?
options: It connects major global energy trade routes
It has the largest landmass in the world
It is the only ocean with no international disputes
It is entirely controlled by India
Paper_Set_083.explanation:
The Indian Ocean region is geopolitically 
significant because it connects the major energy trade 
routes. Petroleum from the Persian Gulf is exported to 
Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Southeast Asian countries, 
China, Japan, and others through Indian Ocean routes. 
The Indian Ocean is the third largest ocean in the world 
after the Pacific and Atlantic Oceans. It lies between the 
continents of Asia, Africa, Australia, and Antarctica. 
The countries of the Indian Ocean region are rich in 
mineral resources. 
The submerged coastal areas of this ocean are rich in 
petroleum and natural gas. Exploration and drilling have 
revealed vast reserves of petroleum and natural gas in 
the Persian Gulf, Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, and along 
the western coast of Australia.

Paper_Set_083.q: Study the following statements regarding sugarcane cultivation in India and select the correct answer using the given codes: 1. It is extensively cultivated in the northern plains. 2. Its production is highest in South India. 3. Its productivity is highest in South India. 4. Sugarcane crushing takes place throughout the year in North India. Codes:
Paper_Set_083.explanation:
The majority of sugarcane cultivation in India 
is in the northern plains. However, South Indian 
sugarcane has a higher sucrose content. In North India, 
sugarcane is sown in summer and harvested in winter.

Paper_Set_083.q: Where is the deposition of pelagic materials found?
Paper_Set_083.explanation:
Pelagic materials are known as "deep-sea 
materials." These are organic deposits formed by algae 
(phytoplankton). They are also referred to as "oozes" 
and are found in deep oceans.

Paper_Set_083.q: Which of the following gases are correctly arranged in descending order of their percentage in air?
Paper_Set_083.explanation:
Nitrogen, Oxygen, Argon, Carbon Dioxide is 
the correct sequence in descending order.

Paper_Set_083.q: Which river flows through the Rift Valley?
Paper_Set_083.explanation: (c) : The Jordan River flows through the Rift Valley, while the Brahmaputra and Yangtze rivers flow through self-formed river valleys.

Paper_Set_083.q: The author of the book 'Geography in the Twentieth Century' is -
Paper_Set_083.explanation:
The author of the book 'Geography in the 
Twentieth Century' is Griffith. Griffith Taylor is 
considered the pioneer of neo-determinism. According 
to him, nature is like a traffic police officer standing at a 
crossroads who controls the travelers at the intersection 
but does not change their destination. 
• Ellsworth Huntington was a strong proponent of 
environmental determinism. 
• Carl O. Sauer was primarily a Possibilist thinker, but 
he also considered Griffith Taylor's concept of neo
determinism to be significant.

Paper_Set_083.q: Which of the following statement about Von Thunen's Model of Agricultural land use is NOT correct?
options: Intensity of land use declines with the distance from the market.
The farmers have a full knowledge of the needs of the market
In Zone-V, one-third of the land is always kept fallow.
In Zone-III, as the distance increases, there is a consequent increase in yield.
Paper_Set_083.explanation:
According to Von Thünen, as the distance 
from the central city (market) increases, land 
productivity and net profit decrease, which results in 
changes in land use or crop patterns. Farmers have full 
knowledge of market needs. In the fifth ring, one-third 
of the land is always left fallow. Von Thünen first 
proposed the localization theory of agriculture in 1826. 
According to his model, in a peripheral region, 
concentric rings of agricultural land use are found 
around the central city in the following order: 
Ring Description 
1st Closest to the city; fruits, vegetables, and dairy 
 are produced. 
2nd Firewood production. 
3rd Intensive agriculture for grains; no land left 
 fallow. 
4th Grain cultivation, some fallow land, some 
 pasture. 
5th More fallow and pasture land, some grains; 
 three-field system exists. 
6th Outermost ring; livestock raising.

Paper_Set_083.q: In which of the following oceans the direction of ocean currents are reversed with season?
Paper_Set_083.explanation:
The India Ocean is unique among the world's 
oceans in that its ocean currents change direction with 
the seasons, a phenomenon primarily driven by the 
monsoon winds. 
• During the summer monsoon, the winds blow from 
the southwest, pushing the surface water towards the 
northeast. 
• During winter monsoon winds reverse and blown 
from northeast to southwest.

Paper_Set_083.q: The dispersion and migration of plants, mainly flowering plants, were started since
options: More than one of the above
Paper_Set_083.explanation: (a) : The spread and migration of plants (mainly flowering plants) first appeared in the Jurassic period but their spread took place in the cretaceous period. The major flowering plants were oak, poplar, Maple and plants similar to modern tropical species. Although there are considerable differences regarding the initial origin of flowering plants, most people consider their origin to be Gondwanaland, from where it spread to various regions.

Paper_Set_083.explanation: See the explanation of the above question.

Paper_Set_083.q: Which state in India produces the highest amount of wheat?
Paper_Set_083.explanation:
Uttar Pradesh is the largest wheat-producing 
state in India. 
• Most of the wheat production in Uttar Pradesh comes 
from the Ganga-Yamuna Doab and Rohilkhand 
plains. 
• 32.8% of the state's cultivated land is used for wheat 
production. 
• Madhya Pradesh ranks second in wheat production. 
• In Punjab, Ludhiana, Sangrur, Firozpur, Faridkot, 
Patiala, and Amritsar contribute to 60% of the state's 
wheat production.

Paper_Set_083.q: Whose work description is "Economic Development with Unlimited Supplies of Labour (1954)"?

W. A. Lewis 
W. A. Lewis wrote the famous paper "Economic

Paper_Set_083.q: Prairie soils are found in:
Paper_Set_083.explanation:
The Prairie region is located in temperate 
zones and has a humid climate. The Prairie grasslands 
are found in North America, where grass height varies 
from east to west. The dominant species is Bluestem 
grass, which grows between 1.5 to 2.4 meters in height,

Paper_Set_083.explanation:
Plank’s Law provides insight into the amount 
of radiation emitted by an object across different 
regions of the electromagnetic spectrum.

Paper_Set_083.explanation:

Paper_Set_083.q: Who propagated the concept of the region as a triad of land, people, and work (employment)?
Paper_Set_083.explanation:
Sir Patrick Geddes proposed the Place-Work
Folk approach for studying human communities. The 
fundamental principle of this approach is that the local 
environment (place) determines the livelihood patterns 
or economic activities of the people living there. The 
sequence of livelihood patterns follows Place-Work
Folk (Family). However, in technologically advanced 
societies, this sequence changes to Folk (Family)
Work-Place. 
Patrick Geddes is considered the founder of regional 
surveys, regionalization, and applied geography in 
Britain. 
Note: Patrick Geddes was the first to use the term 
"conurbation" for a cluster of cities.

Paper_Set_083.q: River capture is more likely to occur when -
options: The slope gradient is the same on both sides of a water divide
There is a significant difference in the slope gradient on both sides of a water divide.
Paper_Set_083.explanation: (d) : When a main river or its tributary captures the water of another river or its tributary, this phenomenon is called river capture. The capturing river is called the 'captor stream', and the river whose water is captured is called the 'captured stream'. River capture activities are more common in the youthful stage and occur under the following conditions: The river slope is steep (high slope gradient), the valley width is narrow, the volume of water is large, the flow velocity is high along with a steep slope, the river flows through weak rock, the river's position is lower relative to others, and the river carries less sediment load. A significant difference in gradient across a divide encourages the more aggressive river (steeper gradient, lower base level) to erode headward and capture the other.

Paper_Set_083.q: The Indus River in the Himalayas is an example of?

not affected by geological changes.

Gilgit, forming a gorge 17,000 feet deep.

example of a consequent drainage pattern.

Paper_Set_084.q: Katabatic wind is
Paper_Set_084.explanation:
Katabatic wind is a downhill wind. At night, 
due to radiation, there is greater loss of heat on mountain 
slopes and upper areas, which makes the air cold. This cold 
and heavy air descends along the slopes into the valleys. 
These are called mountain breezes or katabatic winds. Due 
to these winds, temperature inversion occurs, which results 
in frost or dew formation in valleys at night, while upper 
regions remain frost-free.

wind that moves eastward along the coast disrupts the 
normal upwelling process, which brings cold, nutrient 
rich water to the surface.

the base of the marine food web, leading to a decline in 
fish population and potential collapse of fishing 
industries.

Paper_Set_084.q: Which hills form the northeastern edge of the Chotanagpur Plateau?

Plateau is formed by the Rajmahal Hills. This plateau

by terrestrial coastal relief. The continental shelf 
occupies about 8.6% of the total ocean floor, extending 
over 13.3% of the Atlantic, 5.7% of the Pacific, and 
4.2% of the Indian Ocean.

ranges from 5 to 27% (50 to 270 parts per thousand).

influenced by evaporation and the addition of salt from 
rivers and stream. The high salinity of the GSL is due to 
its being a closed basin, meaning water can only lave 
through evaporation, leaving salts behind.

Paper_Set_085.q: Which of the following statements are NOT correct for the Indian Jute Industry? A. Most the jute producing areas went to Bangladesh, resulting in acute shortage of raw jute. B. Dry climate is very convenient for spinning and weaving Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
Paper_Set_085.explanation:
The jute industry in India began in 1855 AD, 
when George Acland established the first mill at Rishra 
(20 km north of Kolkata). After partition, about 80% of 
the jute-producing area went to East Pakistan (now 
Bangladesh), creating a severe shortage of raw material 
for the industry. In India, around 80% of jute is grown 
in the Ganga–Brahmaputra delta, not 10%, and this 
supplies raw material to the jute mills. The effect of raw 
material availability is clearly seen on the location of 
the jute industry. West Bengal alone produces 81.15% 
of India’s jute. 
The Indian jute industry suffers from many problems 
such as: high cost of production, shortage of raw 
material, increasing competition in the world market, 
lack of modernization in jute mills, and instability in 
production. A dry climate is not very suitable for 
spinning and weaving; rather, the humid climate of 
coastal regions is considered more favorable since 
threads break less in moisture.

Paper_Set_085.q: What are the dark spots (sunspots) that appear on sun surface?
Paper_Set_085.explanation:
Dark spots visible on the surface of the Sun 
(sunspots) are massive magnetic storms. Sunspots are 
regions of the photosphere where the temperature is 
about 1,500°C lower than that of the surrounding areas. 
These spots occur between 5° and 40° north and south 
latitudes of the Sun. The darker central part of a sunspot 
is called the umbra, and the comparatively less dark 
surrounding region is called the penumbra. 
The lifespan of a sunspot ranges from a few hours to 
several months. They appear at intervals of 
approximately 11.1 years, which is also referred to as 
the solar cycle. During the sunspot phase, the magnetic 
field strength ranges from about 100 to 4,000 gauss. 
Once the sunspot dissipates, the magnetic field spreads 
toward the poles.

Paper_Set_087.q: Which ocean current transports warm water from the Gulf of Mexico across the Atlantic Ocean to Western Europe, affecting its climate?

Paper_Set_087.explanation:
The Gulf Stream current carries warm water 
from the Gulf of Mexico across the Atlantic Ocean to 
Western Europe, thereby influencing the climate there. 
Near 45° N latitude and 45° W longitude, the Gulf 
Stream splits into several branches, collectively called 
the North Atlantic Current. One branch flows along the 
coast of Norway (Western Europe) into the Norwegian 
Sea; another, known as the Irminger Current, moves 
toward the southern coast of Iceland; and a third flows 
toward the eastern coast of Greenland. The Gulf Stream 
significantly affects the climate along the eastern coast 
of North America and the coastal regions of 
northwestern Europe. In these areas, the temperature is 
about 4°F higher than the average temperature for their 
latitudes. Due to the Gulf Stream, a temperate climate 
develops in Western Europe, which is why its ports 
remain ice-free throughout the year despite being 
located in high latitudes.

Paper_Set_088.q: The Benioff zone is found along which type of plate boundaries?
Paper_Set_088.explanation: (b) : Destructive plate boundaries – A rigid landmass is called a plate. The study of the nature and movement of these plates is known as plate tectonics. The plate tectonics theory was introduced by Harry Hess in 1960, but its scientific explanation is credited to W.J. Morgan. The Benioff zone is found along destructive plate boundaries. When two plates collide, the denser plate subducts beneath the less dense plate. The region where the plate sinks is called the subduction zone. Since the plate is being destroyed in this area, it is called a destructive plate boundary.

Paper_Set_088.q:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).
 Assertion (A): Antarctica is always covered by snow but receives less than 8 cm of annual precipitation.
 Reason (R): Speedy winds constantly blow in Antarctica.
 Select the correct answer from the code given below:
 Code -
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Paper_Set_088.explanation: (a) : Antarctica is always covered with ice, yet its annual precipitation is less than 8 cm, so the statement is correct. Since Antarctica lies at the South Pole, it receives the least solar radiation, causing extreme cold. The air thus contains very little moisture, leading to minimal precipitation. Strong winds also blow in this region, making the reason correct as well. About 98% of Antarctica is permanently ice-covered. Seasonal variation in ice volume alters the continent’s size, earning it the name dynamic continent. Antarctica is the coldest continent in the world, and its Pole of Cold records the lowest annual temperatures. During the southern solstice, it experiences six months of daylight, and during the northern solstice, six months of night. Lichens and mosses are the main vegetation. Hence, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but (R) does not correctly explain (A).

maximal, because high temperatures and evaporation 
are offset by rainfall, which reduces salinity. The Red

the Gulf of Karabugan, salinity is 17‰. Salinity in the 
Bering Sea is higher compared to the Baltic Sea. 
Generally, the total amount of dissolved solids in one 
kilogram of seawater is called seawater salinity, 
expressed in ‰.

Paper_Set_091.q: Among the four major cities of India, the least temperature variation is observed in:
Paper_Set_091.explanation:
In Mumbai, the maximum temperature in 
January is 22.5°C, while in July, it rises to 27.5°C. In

Paper_Set_091.q: What is the maximum possible population size an ecosystem can support called?
Paper_Set_091.explanation:

average temperatures than those in the Southern 
Hemisphere due to the unequal distribution of land and 
water.

17.2°C.

follow latitude lines.

of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn.

Paper_Set_091.explanation:

Paper_Set_091.q: What was the outcome of the 1997 Kyoto Protocol agreement? (A) 5.2% reduction in carbon dioxide emissions (B) The agreement cannot be invalidated (C) The protocol was to be effective from 1997 (D) The protocol was to be effective from 1999
Paper_Set_091.explanation:
The Kyoto Protocol is an international 
agreement associated with the United Nations 
Framework Convention on Climate Change. It was 
adopted on December 11, 1997, in Kyoto, Japan. 
Although it was supposed to take effect in 1999, it 
officially became operational on February 16, 2005. 
Under the Kyoto Protocol, Annex-I countries were 
committed to reducing their greenhouse gas emissions 
by 5.2% below 1990 levels during 2008–2012.

Paper_Set_091.q: The Aleutian and Mariana trenches were formed by
options: Along the transform fault plate margin
Paper_Set_091.explanation:
The Aleutian and Mariana trenches are 
formed along the convergent plate margins. Convergent 
plate margin are also called destructive plate margins. 
In this, when two plates move towards and collide with 
each other, the heavier plate is sub-ducted beneath the 
lighter plate. Oceanic trenches and volcanic islands are 
formed by the convergence of two oceanic plates.

Paper_Set_091.q: Which are the common indicators used to measure development in geography? A. Gross National Product (GNP) B. Human Development Index (HDI) C. Birth and Death Rate D. Planning Level Choose the correct option:
Paper_Set_091.explanation:
GNP, HDI, and birth & death rates are 
common indicators of development in geography. Gross 
National Product (GNP): The total market value of all 
final goods and services produced by a country’s 
residents within a year. 
• Human Development Index (HDI): Developed by 
economist Mahbub ul Haq in 1990 and published 
annually by the United Nations Development 
Programme (UNDP). It measures life expectancy, 
education levels, and per capita GNP. 
• Birth & Death Rates: 
 ○ Birth rate: Number of live births per 1,000 
people per year. 
 ○ Death rate: Number of deaths per 1,000 people 
per year.

Paper_Set_091.q: Which of the following characterises sustainable development?
options: Complete dependence on and adaptation to the nature
To maintain a balance between economic development and environmental quality
Unrestricted use of non-renewable energy for economic development
More than one of the above
Paper_Set_091.explanation:
Balance between economic development and 
environmental quality is considered a feature of 
sustainable development. Sustainable and equitable human 
development is necessary so that every generation gets 
equal opportunities. All environmental, financial, and 
human resources should be used keeping the future in 
mind. Misuse of any one of these resources will reduce 
opportunities for future generations. The 1987 report Our 
Common Future, also known as the Brundtland Report, 
defined sustainable development as— 
“Development that meets the needs of the present 
generation without compromising the ability of future 
generations to meet their own needs.” 
Therefore, option (b) is correct.

Paper_Set_091.q: In developing countries, the Green Revolution has led to rapid improvements in:
Paper_Set_091.explanation:
The Green Revolution significantly increased 
wheat production, followed by maize and rice. The 
greatest impact was seen in Punjab, Haryana, and 
Western Uttar Pradesh.

Paper_Set_091.q: In which layer of the atmosphere does the ozone layer exist?
Paper_Set_091.explanation:
The ozone layer is present in the 
stratosphere, between 15 to 35 km above the Earth's 
surface. It absorbs the Sun's harmful ultraviolet (UV) 
radiation and protects life on Earth.

Paper_Set_091.q: An official agreement between two sides who are involved in a conflict or argument are termed as a-
Paper_Set_091.explanation:
An official agreement between two sides who 
are involved in a conflict or argument are termed as 
settlement or a treaty. In legal or civil disputes, it is 
termed as a settlement and in international or politics 
conflicts, it is termed as a 'treaty' accord or peace 
agreement.

Paper_Set_091.q: Statement (A): New England industrial region is one of the major industrial regions in the world. Reason (R): The availability of industrial raw materials and transportation facilities is well developed here. Choose the correct answer from the options below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) correctly explains (A).

Paper_Set_091.explanation:

industrial region because industrial raw materials and 
transportation facilities are well-developed here. The 
New England region is located in the northeastern 
United States. The first cotton mill in this region was 
established in 1790. By 1920, 52% of the USA's cotton 
textile industry was concentrated here, but this declined 
to just 15%. The New England industrial region is a 
good example of a dynamic industry because the textile 
industry has now been replaced by metal, machinery, 
chemical, and printing industries.

Paper_Set_091.q: As altitude increases, air temperature generally decreases, but in some special conditions, temperature increases instead. This condition is called—
Paper_Set_091.explanation:

sometimes, due to specific temporal or local factors, the 
temperature increases with altitude. This phenomenon is 
known as temperature inversion.

Paper_Set_091.q: Assertion (A): A thermal anticyclonic condition develops at the 500-millibar level over the Tibetan Plateau during the summer monsoon. Reason (R): The Tibetan Plateau acts as an elevated heat source. Choose the correct answer:

Paper_Set_091.q: Ocean tides are produced as a result of balance between : (1) Centrifugal Force (2) Coriolis Force (3) Gravitational Force (4) Hydraulic agent Force Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
Paper_Set_091.explanation:
Ocean tides are produced as a result of 
balance between gravitational forces and centrifugal 
forces. The moon's gravity and to a lesser extent the 
sun's gravity, pulls on the earth and it's ocean, creating 
bulges of water. The centrifugal force, a result of the 
earth's rotation, works in opposition to the gravitational 
pull farther contributing to the tide formation.

Paper_Set_091.q: Which one of the following is not an approach in Human Geography?
Paper_Set_091.explanation: (c) : The approaches of Human Geography do not include the Quantitative Revolution. However, spatial organization, regional differentiation, exploration, and description are all considered approaches in Human Geography. In the 1820s, French philosopher Auguste Comte proposed Positivism (the basis of the Quantitative Revolution). According to him, true knowledge is scientific and based on facts and experience. In the 1950s, like other sciences, geography came under the strong influence of positivism. Scholars such as McCarty, Schaefer, and Peter Haggett contributed significantly to the development of the Quantitative Revolution in Geography.

Paper_Set_091.q: The rivers flowing in the Himalayan region represent which type of drainage system?
Paper_Set_091.explanation:

was once the Tethys Sea, into which rivers flowed 
from the north. However, after the formation of the 
Himalayas during the Tertiary period, these rivers 
began cutting through the mountain range and flowing 
into the Indian subcontinent. As a result, these are 
termed antecedent rivers. The major antecedent rivers 
include the Indus, Sutlej, and Brahmaputra.

Paper_Set_091.q: 1. The presence of rich placer deposits of gold on the Ghana coast despite complete absence of source rock in the region. 2. Gold veins are in Brazil. 3. Ghana's gold deposits originated from the Brazilian plateau. Select the correct answer using code given below.

emphasizes the study of cultural landscapes formed

Ritter, Friedrich Ratzel, and Otto Gchluter were key

Paper_Set_091.q: Which type of plate boundary is found in the Himalayas between the Indian Plate and the Eurasian Plate?
Paper_Set_091.explanation: (d) : The boundary of the Indian Plate along the Himalayas is a continental-continental convergent type. The Himalayas form the boundary between the Indian Plate in the south and the Eurasian Plate in the north. When two plates move towards each other and collide, the denser plate subducts beneath the less dense one. Since plate destruction occurs here, it is called a destructive plate margin, and such plates are referred to as convergent plates.

Paper_Set_091.q: Cross border terrorism is prevalent on which of the following international borders of India?

Paper_Set_091.q: Where does the Indus River originate?
Paper_Set_091.explanation:

Paper_Set_091.q: Among the schools of thought in human geography, which of the following statement(s) regarding "Possibilism" is/are correct? 1. This theory considers humans as active agents within the environment. 2. Vidal de La Blache was a staunch supporter of the philosophy of possibilism. 3. The concept of possibilism was introduced by Taylor in the 1920s.
Paper_Set_091.explanation:
Possibilism is a French geographical 
ideology developed in the early 20th century that 
emphasizes human efforts and actions in explaining 
human-environment interactions. Blache is regarded as 
the founder of possibilism. Many French geographers 
such as Lucien Febvre, Jean Brunhes, and Demangeon 
strongly supported this concept. Blache considered 
"humans" as the central focus in human-environment 
relationships. According to him, humans are both the 
problem and the solution, while nature serves merely 
as a guide. He emphasized human intelligence, skills, 
and activities and expressed faith in human potential. 
He stated that nature presents various resources and 
opportunities to humans, and they are free to use them. 
According to Blache, "Nature can only be an advisor to 
humans." 
Note: French scholar Lucien Febvre first used the 
term "possibilism" in 1922. He elaborated on the 
concept of possibilism in his book La Terre et 
l'évolution humaine (A Geographical Introduction to 
History).

Paper_Set_091.q:
Arrange the following processes of mass wasting based on movement from slow to fast.

 B. Solifluction
 C. Soil creep 
 D. Earth flow
Paper_Set_091.explanation:
(b) : The following processes of mass wasting are arranged from slowest to fastest movement:
Soil creep → Soil slumping → Earth flow → Mudflow.
When the upper layer of soil is displaced from one place to another by water or wind, it is called soil creep or soil erosion. Soil slumping mostly occurs in periglacial regions. When soil erosion is caused by water or wind, it is called erosion (denudation), also known by other names such as sheet flow, overland flow, mudflow, or debris flow. Mudflow is a collection of fine soil particles mixed with water flowing downslope.
Mass wasting is classified as follows according to movement:
1.Very rapid movement (no water required):
Landslide
Fall
Debris slide
Debris fall
Rock fall
Rock slide
2. Slow movement (requires little water):
Rock creep
Soil creep
Solifluction (in periglacial regions)
3. Rapid movement (requires sufficient water):
Overland flow
Mudflow
Sheet wash

Paper_Set_092.q: What is the significance of the equatorial region in terms of agriculture?
options: Poor soil quality and not suitable for agriculture
It has a diverse range of crops
More than one of the above
Paper_Set_092.explanation:
Poor soil quality, which is not suitable for 
agriculture, is a characteristic of equatorial regions. This 
is because in equatorial areas, high temperatures and 
heavy rainfall lead to intense leaching of the soil. 
During this leaching process, essential nutrients like 
lime (Calcium Carbonate) and Silica are washed away 
with rainwater, leaving behind soils rich in iron oxides 
and aluminium compounds. The high temperatures also 
promote rapid microbial activity, which quickly 
decomposses organic matter and reduces the amount of 
humus in the oil. 
• As a result, the soils in equatorial regions are 
generally not fertile enough for productive agriculture. 
Extensive commerical farming is typically not practiced 
in equatorial zones; instead, it is more option (b) is 
correct, although the BPSC had marked option (c) is 
correct answer.

Westerlies travel from subtropical high pressure belts to subpolar low-pressure belts.
Paper_Set_092.explanation:
Westerlies are permanent winds that blow 
between 30°-35° and 60°-65° latitude in both 
hemispheres. In the Northern Hemisphere, they move 
from the southwest to the northeast, and in the Southern 
Hemisphere, from the northwest to the southeast. Due to 
the abundance of land in the Northern Hemisphere, their 
pattern is more complex, but in the Southern 
Hemisphere, they become extremely strong because of 
the lack of land barriers. These intense winds, often 
accompanied by storms, are called "Roaring Forties" at 
40°S, "Furious Fifties" at 50°S, and "Screaming Sixties" 
at 60°S.

divided the known Earth into five zones: one torrid 
zone, two temperate zones, and two frigid zones. 
He was the first scholar to use a gnomon to measure the 
correct length of the equator and estimated the Earth's 
circumference to be 25,000 miles (actual: 25,860 miles).

distances of the Sun and Moon from the Earth.

geographical knowledge include Thales, Anaximander, 
Hecataeus, Aristotle, Theophrastus, Polybius, and 
Posidonius.

Paper_Set_092.q: Which city is called the “Manchester of India”?
Paper_Set_092.explanation:

up near Kolkata in Fort Gloster in 1818, which failed, 
while the real beginning was in 1854 when a cotton mill 
was established in Mumbai by Cowasjee Nanabhoy

Mumbai is called “Cottonopolis of India.” Note: Tamil 
Nadu has the most textile mills, producing 42.2% of the

Paper_Set_092.q: In winter, the position of the subtropical jet stream fluctuates between which latitudes?
Paper_Set_092.explanation:
During winter, the position of the subtropical 
jet stream fluctuates between 20° and 35° N latitude. 
The subtropical jet stream is located in the upper 
troposphere above the subtropical high-pressure belt 
(30°–35° latitude). It flows from west to east and is 
more stable than the polar front jet stream.

Paper_Set_092.q: The Garo, Khasi, and Jaintia Hills of Meghalaya are structurally related to –
Paper_Set_092.explanation:

resemble those of the Chota Nagpur Plateau. Initially, 
this plateau was connected to the main plateau, but it 
separated during the formation of the Bay of Bengal. 
Therefore, these hills are structurally related to the 
Peninsular Plateau.

Paper_Set_092.q:
Assertion (A): Most geomorphic processes originate in the Earth's atmosphere and are driven by gravitational force.
 Reason (R): Therefore, gravity is a geomorphic process.

Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Paper_Set_092.explanation: (b) : Most geomorphic processes originate in the Earth's atmosphere and are driven by gravitational force. Thus, both the assertion and reason are stated as correct in the source explanation, but they do not explain each other. (Note: Geomorphologists usually classify gravity as a force driving mass wasting, rather than a process itself).

Paper_Set_092.q: The subsequent drainage generally occurs:
options: In accordance with the consequent drainage
At a right angle to the consequent drainage
Paper_Set_092.explanation:
The subsequent drainage generally occurs at 
a right angle to the consequent drainage. 
• In any region, the formation of a consequent river 
happens first. Consequent rivers follow the 
regional slope and are also known as dip streams. 
In folded mountainous regions, consequent rivers 
originate in synclinal troughs and are termed 
synclinal consequent rivers.

Paper_Set_092.q: In which region is the salinity of seawater the highest?
Paper_Set_092.explanation:
Subtropical regions have high salinity due to 
low rainfall and high evaporation.

Paper_Set_092.q: Arrange the following Natural Hazards/ Disasters of India in chronological order (earlier to latest): A. Tsunami (off Tamil Nadu Coast) B. Bhuj Earthquake C. Super Cyclone of Orissa D. Koyna Earthquake Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
Paper_Set_092.explanation:
The chronological order (oldest to latest) of 
the given natural disasters/hazards in India is: 
• Koyna Earthquake (1967 AD) → Odisha Super 
Cyclone (1999 AD) → Bhuj Earthquake (2001 AD) → 
Tsunami (Tamil Nadu coast, 2004 AD). 
In the past, India has suffered huge losses of life and 
property due to several devastating earthquakes, such as 
Koyna (1967), Uttarkashi (1991), Latur (1993), and 
Bhuj (2001). 
In India, tropical cyclones mainly cause heavy losses of 
life and property in coastal areas. These cyclones are 
mostly formed over the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian 
Sea between 8°N and 15°N latitudes. 
The Odisha Super Cyclone of October 29, 1999 killed 
more than 11,000 people, and about one-third of Odisha 
was submerged with saline water. 
The cyclone of June 9, 1998 killed 1261 people in Gujarat. 
The largest tsunami disaster in Indian history occurred 
on 26 December 2004, caused by an 8.9 magnitude 
earthquake near the Sumatra coast of Indonesia, killing 
about 1.5 lakh people in Asia and Africa (including 
15,160 in India).

Paper_Set_092.q: The activity of ITCZ (Intertropical Convergence Zone) primarily determines the duration of rainfall in:
Paper_Set_092.explanation:
The shift of the Intertropical Convergence 
Zone (ITCZ) occurs due to the movement of the sun 
between the Northern and Southern Hemispheres, 
which also influences the Southern Oscillation. As a 
result, the Indian monsoon is controlled by the ITCZ, 
determining the duration of monsoon rainfall in India.

Paper_Set_092.q: In which district of Rajasthan is gypseous soil found?
Paper_Set_092.explanation:
Gypseous soil is found in the Bikaner district 
of Rajasthan. This soil is mainly found in the north
western parts of Rajasthan. It is classified into two 
types: Petrogypsic and Haplogypsic soils. 
● Petrogypsic soil consists of hard gypsum nodules and 
is surrounded by high sand dunes. It has a high 
content of calcium carbonate and sand. 
● Haplogypsic soil is found in the depressions between 
large sand dunes. Its depth varies from 50-70 cm and 
contains fine, calcium-free sand. It has amorphous 
gypsum and is permeable to water.

Paper_Set_092.q: The doldrums are found in which pressure belt?
Paper_Set_092.explanation:
The doldrums extend 5° north and south of 
the equator. This region has low atmospheric pressure 
and little horizontal air movement, making it a calm 
wind belt. Due to the rising air currents, it is also known 
as the "calm belt."

Paper_Set_092.q: Which of the following landforms is not associated with river deposition?
Paper_Set_092.explanation: (b) : A meander is formed due to river erosion, whereas natural levees, alluvial fans, and talus cones are results of deposition.

Paper_Set_092.q: How long does it take for a location to complete two cycles of high and low tides?
Paper_Set_092.explanation:
It takes more than 24 hours to complete two 
cycles of high and low tides at a given location. 
Generally, there are two tides in a day. Since the Earth 
rotates on its axis once in about 24 hours, one might 
expect tides to occur every 12 hours. However, in 
reality, tides occur approximately 26 minutes later each 
day because the Moon is also orbiting the Earth while 
the Earth rotates on its axis.

Paper_Set_093.q: Give below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A) : Arhar, being a leguminous crop, help in restoring soil fertility. Reason (R) : Arhar is mostly grown in rotation with other crops. choose the correct answer from the option given below:
options: (A) and (R) both are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) and (R) both are true but (R) is not correct explanation of (A)
Paper_Set_093.explanation:
• Assertion (A) : Arhar, being a leguminous 
crop, helps in restaring soil fertility. Yes, Arhar (Pigeon 
Pea) is a leguminous crop. Leguminous crops fix 
atmospheric nitrogen into the soil through symbiotic 
bacteria in their root nodules (Rhizobium). 
This process enriches soil nitrogen and thus restores soil 
fertility. 
• Reason (R) : Arhar is mostly grown in rotation with 
other crops. 
 Yes, Arhar is commonly grown in crop rotation 
systems with Cereals and other crops. Crops rotation 
helps in reducing pest buildup and maintaing soil 
health. 
• Does (R) explain (A) ? 
 No, while (R) is true, it does not explain why Arhar 
restores soil fertility. Crop rotation is a farming 
practice, but the reason Arhar restores soil fertility is 
nitrogen fixation, which is unrelased to rotation. 
 Rotation is beneficial but not the cause of soil 
fertility restoration by Arhar.

Paper_Set_094.q: The Number of parallels of latitudes & meridians of longitudes on the globe are
options: More than one of the above
Paper_Set_094.explanation: (e) : Latitudes and longitudes are imaginary lines drawn on a globe. Latitudes are also called parallels. The globe is divided into two equal halves by an imaginary line called the Equator. The half north of the equator is the Northern Hemisphere, and the half south of it is the Southern Hemisphere. Both hemispheres have 90°–90° latitudes, and including the 0° latitude (Equator), the total number of latitudes is 181, while the number of latitude lines is 179. Longitudes are imaginary lines drawn vertically on the globe. The 0° longitude is called the Prime Meridian. The eastern side of it is called Eastern Longitude, and the western side is called Western Longitude. There are 180 longitudes east and 180 west, making a total of 360 longitudes. Hence, option (e) is correct.

Paper_Set_095.q: What is believed to have triggered the collapse of the solar nebula according to nebular hypothesis?

Due to gravity, these particles collided with each other, generating heat. This created angular momentum, causing them to rotate. Thus, originally cold and motionless matter gradually became a large, hot nebula. Hence, option (b) is correct.

Reason (R): The ITCZ is generally located on or near the meteorological equator. Codes:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) correctly explains (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) does not correctly explain (A).
Paper_Set_096.explanation:
According to Flohn, the convergence of trade 
winds results in the formation of marginal zones around 
the equatorial calm belt, known as the Intertropical 
Convergence Zone (ITCZ). Due to seasonal changes in the 
Sun’s position, the ITCZ shifts accordingly. In July, it 
moves northward, forming the Northern ITCZ, and in 
January, it shifts southward, forming the Southern ITCZ.

Paper_Set_096.q: In contrast to Mackinder's Heart land Theory, Spykman's Rimland Theory emphasies which regions strategic importance?
Paper_Set_096.explanation:
Contrary to Mackinder’s Heartland Theory, 
Spykman’s Rimland Theory emphasizes the strategic 
importance of the coastal marginal areas of Eurasia. 
In his book “The Geography of Peace”, Spykman 
explained his concept of the Rimland or the Periphery. 
He firmly believed that in contemporary world politics, 
the basis of international strategic relations lies in 
maritime power, not in the future possibilities of 
Heartland development. Spykman’s Rimland included 
continental Europe west of the Baltic and Black Sea 
isthmus, the mountainous, southwestern, and 
southeastern regions of Asia, and China. He criticized 
Mackinder’s theory of Heartland dominance as flawed 
and put forth a new strategic formula: 
“Who controls the Rimland rules Eurasia; who rules 
Eurasia controls the destinies of the world.”

Paper_Set_096.q: Which of the following has a biomass pyramid in a grassland ecosystem?
Paper_Set_096.explanation:
The biomass pyramid in a grassland or crop 
ecosystem is upright. 
The number of organisms in a food pyramid shows the 
number of primary producers and different levels of 
consumers in an ecosystem. The base of this pyramid 
always indicates the number of producers. The pyramid 
becomes upright when the number of producers is 
highest and the number of consumers decreases 
progressively. In contrast, it becomes inverted when 
there is only one producer and the number of consumers 
increases.

Paper_Set_096.q: Noctilucent clouds are found in which sphere of the atmsophere?
Paper_Set_096.explanation:
In the mesosphere layer of the atmosphere, 
noctilucent clouds are found. The mesosphere extends 
from 50 to 80 km above sea level. These clouds are 
observed over the poles during summer. They form 
through the condensation caused by meteoric dust and 
moisture brought upward by convective processes. 
The lowest layer of the atmosphere is called the 
troposphere or the "zone of change." The term 
"troposphere" was coined by Léon Teisserenc de Bort. 
The layer above the tropopause is called the 
stratosphere. This layer was first discovered and studied 
by Léon Teisserenc de Bort. 
The ionosphere in the atmosphere extends from 80 km 
to 640 km above sea level.

Paper_Set_096.q: How many stages are there in demographic transition?
Paper_Set_096.explanation:
The demographic transition model typically 
has four stages- 
• Stage 1 : High birth and death rates, resulting in slow 
population growth. 
• Stage 2 : Death rates fall, but birth rates remain high, 
leading to rapid population growth. 
• Stage 3 : Birth rates begin to fall, slowing down 
population growth. 
• Stage 4 : Birth and death rates are both low, resulting 
in a stable or slow-growing population

activity. It was propounded by Blache. Blache firmly 
believed that a human community, living for several 
generations in the same type of environment, develops 
a distinctive and often unique way of life, customs, and 
values through collective efforts, which become an 
integral part of the community’s mentality. Blache 
termed this collectively developed mindset, way of 
life, and value system as ‘Genre de vie.’

Paper_Set_096.q: Which waves can propagate in core region?
Paper_Set_096.explanation: (a) : Primary wave. Primary waves can pass through all three mediums, solid, liquid and gas. For this reason only P waves can propagate in intermediate region of core. Paper_Set_097.q: Which of the following statements about seawater are correct? (a) The density of seawater depends on temperature, pressure, and salinity. (b) Water convergence has no effect on density. (c) Thermal expansion of water changes with temperature fluctuations. (d) Due to excessive rainfall in mid-latitudes, density increases. Select the correct answer: (a) Only
Paper_Set_097.explanation:
Only (a) and (c) are correct. 
Water convergence affects density (so statement (b) is 
false). 
In mid-latitudes, high rainfall causes a decrease in 
density, not an increase. 
Density is influenced by temperature, pressure, and 
salinity: 
Temperature → Thermal expansion 
Pressure → Compressibility 
Salinity → Dissolved elements 
Pure water density = 1.000 g/cm³ (at 4°C) 
Average ocean water density = 1.0278 g/cm³, 2-3% 
higher than pure water.

Paper_Set_097.q: Which of the following mountain ranges of Peninsular India has the highest peak ?
Paper_Set_097.explanation:
The highest peak of Peninsular India is 
Anamudi (2695 m), located in the Anamalai Hills of the 
Western Ghats. The Western Ghats extend for about 
1600 km, from the Tapi River in the north to Cape 
Comorin (Kanyakumari) in the south. The Vindhyan 
range separates the vast northern plains from the rest of 
Peninsular India. It stretches for about 1050 km from 
Jobat in Gujarat to Sasaram in Bihar. The Aravalli range 
extends for about 800 km in a northeast–southwest 
direction between Delhi and Palanpur (Gujarat). Its 
highest peak is Guru Shikhar (1722 m), located at 
Mount Abu. The Satpura range extends about 900 km 
from Ratnapur in the west to Amarkantak in the east. Its 
highest peak is Dhoopgarh (1350 m), located in the 
Mahadeo Hills.

Paper_Set_097.q: Which one of the followings forms on cold surfaces when condensation takes place freezing point temperature?
Paper_Set_097.explanation:
Frost forms on cold surfaces when 
condensation takes place below freezing point (0ºC), 
i.e., the dew point is at or below the freezing point. 
When the dew point is at or below freezing point, under 
above mentioned conditions, the condensation of extra 
moisture takes place in the form of very minute 
particles of ice crystals. It is known as frost. In this 
process, the excess moisture is deposited in the form of 
minute ice crystals instead of water droplets.

Paper_Set_097.q: Which of the following is formed due to tectonic forces?
Paper_Set_097.explanation: (a) : Rift valleys are formed due to tectonic tension forces that cause blocks of the Earth’s crust to move along fault lines, creating a deep valley.

Paper_Set_097.q: Identify the statements which are NOT correct about frontiers and boundaries. A. Boundaries are two dimensional while frontiers are three dimensional. B. Boundaries are ‘de facto’ while frontiers are ‘de jure’. C. Boundaries are maintained by state and has no material existence. D. Frontiers occupy a fixed position and their boundaries can not be altered. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
Paper_Set_097.explanation:
• A frontier lies between two social or political 
entities and has a real, physical presence. 
• A boundary is a line marking sovereignty; it is usually 
legal (de jure) and may not have a physical presence.

are two-dimensional.

geographic, economic, political, or demographic 
changes.

warming, acid rain, and health issues. Geothermal,

Paper_Set_097.explanation:

Paper_Set_097.q: Which is the most abundant pelagic deposit found in the Indian Ocean?
Paper_Set_097.explanation:
The most common pelagic deposit in the 
Indian Ocean is Globigerina Ooze. The word Jattugm is 
derived from the German word Jattude, meaning “sea.” 
Thus, pelagic deposits are those that accumulate on the 
ocean floor and originate in seawater itself. Pelagic 
deposits are of two types – (1) Biogenic deposits, and 
(2) Abiogenic deposits. Biogenic deposits contain 
remains of organisms and plants. These are classified 
into two categories – (1) calcareous deposits, and (2) 
siliceous deposits. Calcareous deposits are further 
divided into two types: 
Hydrosphere 315(a) Pteropod ooze 
(b) Globigerina ooze 
Globigerina ooze originates from the skeletal remains 
of calcareous organisms, primarily Globigerina. Hence, 
it is called Globigerina ooze. This ooze contains 
64.47% calcium, 1.64% silica, and 3.33% mineral 
elements. It is found at depths of 3000 to 4000 fathoms. 
It occurs extensively in the warm waters of the tropical 
and temperate Atlantic Ocean. It is also found along the 
eastern and western continental margins of the Indian 
Ocean and in the western Pacific Ocean.
